chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A group came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said, “Peace be upon you, our Lord.” So he asked them to repent, but they did not repent. Then he dug for them a pit and kindled a fire in it, and he dug another pit beside it and opened a passage between them. Then, when they did not repent, he cast them into the pit and kindled a fire in the other pit until they died.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports do not contradict the earlier ones concerning that the apostate is not asked to repent, because the earlier reports apply to one who was born upon the fiṭrah of Islam and then apostatized; his repentance is not accepted and he is killed in every case. The later reports apply to one who had been a disbeliever, then accepted Islam, then apostatized after that; such a person is asked to repent, and if he repents within three days, otherwise he is killed. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام has detailed what we have mentioned in what ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from him, and we have already presented it, and what he narrated further confirms that:

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers; here part of the title Amīr al-Muʾminīn for Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدَّ: the apostate; one who turns back from Islam
key_terms.تَوْبَتُهُ: his repentance; return from error or unbelief
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: three days; the period mentioned for repentance in one category
key_terms.رَبَّنَا: our Lord; a statement of divinization directed toward the Imam
key_terms.فَاسْتَتَابَهُمْ: he asked them to repent from their false belief
key_terms.فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the natural state of Islam; here meaning one born into Islam
key_terms.كَافِرًا: a disbeliever; one outside Islam before accepting it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on different types of apostasy and repentance?
ai.summary: This report recounts an incident involving people who addressed Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام with divinizing language, after which he called them to repentance and punished them when they refused. It is followed by a legal clarification distinguishing between different categories of apostasy: one born Muslim who apostasizes, and one who enters Islam after disbelief and then apostasizes. The passage is significant for its treatment of shirk-like exaggeration regarding the Imam and for its juristic differentiation in rulings on the apostate.
